transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. It's been pretty frustrating. 

I'm a jeweler, and lately when I'm at the bench, I just... I jump around too much. I'll go from reading a customer email to looking at a saw mark on a piece of metal, and then a noise outside catches my attention. Next thing I know, I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order I was supposed to be doing. I just can't seem to keep my focus.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility your entire life, or is this a new problem that has developed more recently?

No, it's definitely not a lifelong thing. It's a pretty new problem. This whole wired, kind of out-of-control stretch really just started right after I got an award at a jewelry show recently. And, um, it went on like that for about two weeks.
During those two weeks, did you experience any unusual thoughts, or hear or see things that other people didn't seem to notice?

No, nothing like that. Um, I didn't see or hear anything that wasn't there. My thoughts were definitely moving way too fast, but they weren't really unusual or weird. It was just normal work stuff and everyday things, just... a lot of it all at once. I definitely wasn't hearing voices or anything.
In the past, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in almost all of your usual activities?

Yeah, actually... that's kind of where I'm at right now. These past couple weeks, I just wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like the shine has just completely gone out of everything. I don't even care about being at the bench. Honestly, I've even sat in my truck and just cried before going in to open the shop. It's been pretty bad.
How much has this recent heavy, hollow feeling interfered with your ability to get through your daily responsibilities or maintain your relationships?

It's interfered a lot, honestly. At work, I actually missed a major custom delivery recently. My shop records just got so disorganized that I finally had to stop taking any new work for now. I just can't keep up with it. And as for my family... well, they've been checking on me a lot more lately. I guess they got pretty worried seeing how far I've slipped from my usual routines.
During these past few weeks, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or that you would be better off dead?

Yeah, I have. Um... I keep having these thoughts that my family and my clients would just be better off if I wasn't around anymore. I don't have a plan or anything to actually do it, but... it honestly scares me how often the thought comes up lately.

During that two-week period when you felt 'wired' and your thoughts were racing, did you require any hospitalization, or did your behavior become so erratic that it caused serious problems in your relationships or work that were noticeable to others?

I didn't go to the hospital, no. But as for causing problems... well, it's kind of like what I mentioned a minute ago. That period is actually when my shop records got so completely disorganized. It caused me to miss that major custom delivery, and things got so out of hand that I had to stop taking any new work for now just to try and fix it. 

And yeah, it was definitely noticeable to others. That's when my family really started checking on me more, because they got pretty worried seeing how far I'd slipped from my usual routines.
During that two-week period when you felt wired and your thoughts were racing, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Yeah, I did. For a while during that time, I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up completely clear-headed... I'd just get right out of bed, really excited to start cutting stones or posting my new designs online way before sunrise. I just didn't feel like I needed any more rest than that.
During those two weeks when you were sleeping very little and your thoughts were racing, did you feel unusually 'up,' euphoric, or perhaps more irritable than is typical for you?

Yeah, I definitely felt both. Right after a jewelry show I did around then, I just felt... lit up, I guess. Like I was larger than life one minute. But then, if anyone told me I needed to slow down or tried to get me to stick to normal shop hours, I would just snap right at them. I was definitely way more irritable than usual if people tried to get in my way.

During these past few weeks when you've felt this heavy and hopeless, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite, your ability to concentrate, or your physical movements, such as feeling like you're moving in slow motion or feeling unable to sit still?

I haven't really noticed much change with my appetite or how I'm moving around. But my concentration is just... it's really bad right now. It's been pretty frustrating at work. I'll just sit and stare at a repair ticket, or like, a tray of sapphires, and I just can't hold the measurements in my head long enough to even decide what I'm supposed to do next.
During those two weeks when you were feeling 'lit up' and racing, did you ever feel so overwhelmed or out of control that you had thoughts about harming yourself?

Not really during that time when I was racing, no. But lately... with how down and heavy I've been feeling, yeah. I keep having these thoughts that my family, and even my clients at the shop, would just be better off if I wasn't around. I don't have an actual plan to do anything, but... it honestly scares me how often that thought comes up in my head right now.
In the past few weeks, have you felt so physically slowed down that it was difficult to carry out simple tasks, or conversely, have you felt so restless that you were unable to sit still?

No, not really. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I haven't really noticed much of a change in how I'm physically moving around. I don't feel slowed down to the point where I can't do simple things, and I'm not feeling restless or jittery either. My body feels normal, I guess... it's really just that heavy feeling and the bad concentration I'm dealing with.

During these past few weeks when you have been feeling down, have you found that you are unable to perform your daily tasks, such as basic self-care, or are you still managing to get dressed and take care of your personal needs?

I'm still managing to get dressed and take care of myself. I mean, it takes a bit more effort than usual to get out of bed and get ready for work, but I'm still doing it. I haven't stopped showering or brushing my teeth or anything like that. I'm just... doing it all while feeling really heavy.

During those two weeks when you were feeling 'lit up' and racing, did you feel like you were able to function at your job or in your personal life, even though you were disorganized, or was your behavior so extreme that you were completely unable to carry out your normal day-to-day activities?

Well, I definitely wasn't functioning normally. I mean, I was doing a lot, but none of it was actually productive. I missed a major deadline for a custom piece I was making, which is a big deal in my line of work. And my shop records... they got so completely disorganized that I've actually had to stop taking on any new work just to try and sort out the mess. My family noticed it too. They started checking in on me a lot more because they were worried about how far off my usual routines I had gotten. So, yeah, it definitely messed up my day-to-day life.

Looking back over your life before these recent events, have you ever experienced any other periods where you felt this 'lit up' and racing, or conversely, any other times where you felt this heavy and hopeless?

No, I don't think so. I mean, this is the first time I've ever felt quite like this—either the racing part or this heavy feeling I have right now. Before all this started recently, everything was just... normal, I guess. I haven't had anything like this happen before.
